title: Remove Colored Pieces if Both Neighbors are the Same Color
summary: Given a line of n pieces colored 'A' or 'B', Alice and Bob take turns removing pieces.
statement: Given a line of n pieces colored 'A' or 'B', Alice and Bob take turns removing pieces. Alice can only remove 'A' pieces if both neighbors are 'A', and Bob can only remove 'B' pieces if both neighbors are 'B'. Neither can remove edge pieces. If a player cannot make a move, they lose. Assuming optimal play, determine if Alice wins.
constraints: Alice removes an interior A with A neighbors; Bob similarly removes B, and Alice moves first.
Return whether Alice wins under optimal play.
hints: Removing inside a same-color run shortens only that run and never creates choices in another run.
A run of length L contributes max(0,L-2) moves to its owner; compare total Alice and Bob moves.
Scan runs, accumulate length-2 for A or B, return A_moves>B_moves.
Each move consumes one independent available interior; alternating turns means Alice wins exactly when her move supply is strictly larger.
editorial: Each move consumes one independent available interior; alternating turns means Alice wins exactly when her move supply is strictly larger.

tests.explanation: Alice has one available removal and Bob has none, so Alice wins.
Neither player can remove a piece, so Alice loses.
